children: Seasonally adjusted electronic card transactions in New Zealand dropped 0.9% month-on-month in August 2026, reversing a downwardly revised 1.2% rise in the previous month.

The decline was weighed down by lower spending on hospitality (-1.7% vs 2.4% in July), durables (-1.6% vs 2.0%), apparel (-2.0% vs 3.2%), and consumables (-0.4% vs 1.0%), while motor vehicle spending declined at a faster pace (-0.3% vs -0.2%).
In contrast, fuel spending rose 1.3% after falling 4.2% in July.
On an annual basis, total electronic card spending edged up 0.2%, easing sharply from a 3.4% gain in July and marking the softest increase since December 2025, when spending declined 0.5%.

title: New Zealand Credit Card Spending Falls 0.9% in August
